industry.why: Neutral, carried, balanced on new evidence both ways. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses call a cyclical upturn, DNB Carnegie (22 Oct) reading Sandvik and Metso as a new mining cycle and Danske (18 Oct) heavy trucks and pulp and paper turning, and Goldman's economists (16 Oct) have US industrial production beating with machinery and electrical equipment near peak capacity use; against it, Danske's own warning that most cyclical exposure is 'more or less at all-time highs' with 'cost inflation emerging', a risk-off regime confirmed on all five defensive windows, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior at industry level. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment and grid, Diversified groups, Distributors and Test and measurement at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Counter-case for B: the order data are the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack; for D: the tape and the regime.

memo.verdict: Park. Neutral at 138.00 EUR (price as at 2026-10-08); conviction medium, a working hypothesis at Triaging depth. The record is bullish on the business and neutral on the shares: the stock is a buy at 129 EUR and a hold at 138 EUR, and the difference is the multiple the market will not yet pay for a franchise whose terminal value is in debate. The gate line does not bite (management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability B); the park is on the return, not on the quality. Two dated triggers to re-open at Early-Stage: (1) price at or below about 130 EUR, where the eighteen-month modal return clears 20 percent a year on the record's path with the multiple at the ten-year median; (2) the Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-05 showing data-centre organic growth above 25 percent, Europe no worse than minus 1 percent and working capital turning, which would raise the record's odds on the multiple branch above 40 percent and move the return into the B band at the current price. The case is invalidated rather than parked if FY2026 free cash flow comes in below 12 percent of sales and Q3 2026 data-centre organic growth is below 20 percent.
case: - Legrand is a quality compounder with a structural demand inflection in the third of it that serves data centres and a cyclical trough in the rest. At 138.00 EUR the shares pay for the compounding (about 15 percent a year over eighteen months) and not for the price; the multiple has nowhere obvious to go until the market's doubt about the outer years of the data-centre niche is answered. So the case is a C against the 20 percent bar; it becomes a B at about 130 EUR, or at 138 EUR if the doubt lifts.

- The change is external and structural and has travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain: resources (three new Executive Committee members), choices (the 2030 targets raised 2026-09-29), actions (seven acquisitions in H1 2026 adding about 450 million EUR of sales at about 11 to 12 times EBIT; a first divestment programme), key operating metrics (group organic growth 9.8 percent against a history of about 3 percent), financial statements (H1 sales plus 13.1 percent), sell-side estimates (FY2028 EPS up 14.7 percent over twelve months to 2026-10-02). The force is sector-level: global data-centre capacity projected from 87 GW in 2025 to 233 GW by 2030; content per megawatt from 2.5 million USD to 3.3 million USD; Schneider Electric's triple-digit data-centre order growth in Q2 2026; order intake 'very strong' with pipeline discussions into 2029.

- The internal change is an acceleration under the same leadership, not a break: guidance raised at every level within twelve months (KQ 4 Guidance raised is the one A among the twelve internal forces), acquisition spending to about 60 percent of free cash flow, leverage to 2.24 times EBITDA inside a new 1.5 to 2.5 times envelope. 'Change Forces' B not A: the strongest force acts on a third of the company, no chief-executive change, no strategy break, no new pricing power beyond the established 1 to 2 percent a year (pricing plus 2.9 percent in H1 2026 against about 4 percent purchase inflation; long-run plus 1.5 percent a year; guided about plus 1 percent a year to 2030). One screen red flag live: rising leverage funding acquisitions.
counter_case: - The 'False Friend', the risks research's own winner on internal consistency, carried at full force at the head of 'Investment Thesis': record near-term data-centre hypergrowth and a record backlog mask two structural problems that arrive after the backlog is delivered.

- The building core, about 60 percent of sales, is ex-growth: ten quarters of negative volume and a historical organic growth rate of 3 percent against 5.4 percent at Schneider Electric; Legrand's organic growth lagged electrification peers by 420 basis points over 2020 to 2025.
triggers: - Q3 2026 results, 2026-11-05: the first quarter after the Capital Markets Day and the comparison with the Q3 2025 organic miss. Re-open trigger: data-centre organic growth above 25 percent, Europe no worse than minus 1 percent, working capital turning. Alarm: organic growth below 7 percent; data-centre organic below 20 percent. Invalidate: a guidance cut; data-centre organic below 15 percent for two consecutive quarters.

- Price: at or below about 130 EUR (129 EUR on the arithmetic) the eighteen-month modal return clears 20 percent a year on the record's path at 19.7 times; the case is a buy at 129 EUR and a hold at 138 EUR.

- FY2026 results, early 2027: free cash flow back to the guided 13 to 15 percent of sales (consensus 1,480 million EUR, 13.4 percent). Alarm below 12 percent of sales; invalidate below 10 percent for the full year. Together with Q3 data-centre growth below 20 percent this invalidates rather than parks.

- The power sidecar's commercial launch in 2027: the hard evidence that the concern is clearing and the first of the two conditions (about 70 percent) behind the 40 percent multiple branch; slipping past 2027 changes the record's mind.

- Native 800 volt DC: a named hyperscaler standardising before 2028 (the Alarm level on enclosure) changes the record's mind; a solid-state transformer launched ahead of the 2H27 timeline, or a server OEM announcing native-DC standardisation, is the fundamental shock. Invalidate: data-centre revenue falling beyond the 11 percent net headwind.

- The European building recovery: French and German permits and starts monthly, Eurozone construction confidence; Europe organic growth quarterly. Modal: Europe flat in 2027, plus 2 to 3 percent in 2028. Alarm: Europe organic below minus 3 percent in a quarter. Invalidate: permits negative year-on-year through Q4 2027.
